title: Pattern Matching in Ruby
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of pattern matching in ruby in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply pattern matching in ruby in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to pattern matching versus conditional checks and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Pattern Matching in Ruby through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding pattern matching in ruby helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Pattern Matching in Ruby helps you reason about case and in. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: case and in. Then connect it to Array and hash patterns. The remaining syllabus points—Matching nested structures, Pattern matching versus conditional checks—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Pattern Matching in Ruby
content_blocks.code:
point = {x: 3, y: 4}
case point
in {x: Integer => x, y: Integer => y} if x == y - 1
  puts "diagonal step"
else
  puts "other point"
end
